<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When a DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1 response is cut by `max_tokens` inside a DSML tool call, the Rust frontend returns the half-written markup as `content`, for example `…\n<｜DSML｜ invoke name="get_weather"` with `finish_reason=length`. This PR adds `ToolParserError::IncompleteToolCall` and drops the buffered text only for that error at `max_tokens`. Related: #62051 (Python parser, same class of problem), #62259.

## Claims

- A tool call cut by `max_tokens` no longer appears in `content`: DSML in content goes from 22/88 to 0/88 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Earlier text and completed calls are kept.
- For every other finish reason (stop, EOS, a stop string), and for any other parser error, the buffered text still falls back to content, as before. The existing Gemma4 EOS-recovery test passes unchanged.
- With thinking on, reasoning that was emitted before the cut is kept, and only the unfinished markup is dropped: DSML in content goes from 32 and 35 / 154 on two base runs to 0 / 154.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (Rust 1.95, `main` @ `953fa442`; the same counts on `83c9a547`):

| Crate | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `rust/src/parser` | 578 passed | 583 passed |
| `rust/src/chat` | 357 passed | 361 passed |

`cargo fmt --check` is clean on the 6 touched files.

New tests:
- DSML cut at 4 positions, each at every two-chunk split. The positions are inside a parameter, inside `invoke`, inside the opener, and after `<｜DS`. In every case the earlier text is emitted, `finish()` returns `IncompleteToolCall`, and `reset()` holds only the unfinished markup.
- V3.2 and V4: a half-written opener (`<｜DSML｜function_ca`, `<｜DSML｜tool_ca`) returns `IncompleteToolCall`. The open-block case is covered by the existing V3.2 tests.
- A completed call followed by a truncated one: the first call is returned with its arguments.
- Ordinary trailing text is kept.
- `unified.rs`, four cases:
  - `IncompleteToolCall` at `length` drops only the buffer, and the reasoning and text emitted before it are kept;
  - a tool call that was already emitted is kept;
  - a different finish error at `length` still falls back to content;
  - with the real `CombinedParser` (DeepSeek reasoning parser plus the V4.1 DSML parser), `<think>plan</think>` followed by a cut inside the opener: at `stop` the half opener falls back to content, at `length` it is dropped. In both cases the reasoning `plan` is kept. This also checks that `IncompleteToolCall` is still recognised after `CombinedParser` wraps it.

**End-to-end.** Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4×H200 with TP4, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`.
- `deepseek_dsml/mod.rs` and `tool/error.rs` are identical in 92044241 and `main`.
- The PR build applies the non-test hunks to 92044241. Its `unified.rs` differs from `main` only in an unrelated `timestamps` field.
- Each request has a `get_weather` tool. Greedy plus T=1.0 / top_p 0.95, streaming and non-streaming.

| Case | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Thinking off, cut by `max_tokens` 20 / 40 / 80 / 160 (88): DSML in `content` | 22 / 88 | **0 / 88** |
| Thinking off, cut by a stop string inside the call (`</｜DSML｜ parameter>` / `</｜DSML｜ invoke>`, 44, `finish_reason=stop`): falls back to `content` | yes (24 / 44 with DSML) | yes (27 / 44 with DSML) |
| Thinking on, `max_tokens` 20 / 40 / 80 / 160 / 320 with the tool, 20 / 40 without (154): DSML in `content` | 32 / 154 and 35 / 154 (two runs) | **0 / 154** |
| Same 154: empty `reasoning_content` | 30 and 35 (two runs) | 37 |

- In the stop-string rows, both builds fall back to content. The counts differ only by sampling: in the other requests the model declined to call the tool and answered in plain text.
- Untruncated tool calls still return valid arguments.
- Greedy outputs are not reproducible across server restarts here: two runs of the unchanged base build agree on 8 of 14 greedy samples. So the thinking-on rows compare counts, and the unit test above covers the reasoning check deterministically.

## Details

- **Root cause:**
  - `DeepSeekDsmlToolParser::finish()` fails while a tool-call block is open (`deepseek_dsml/mod.rs`).
  - The unified output path (`rust/src/chat/src/output/default/unified.rs`) handles a failed `finish()` by emitting `parser.reset()` as text, so the unconsumed DSML ends up in `content`.
  - The `calls` opener was already consumed, which is why the leaked text starts at `<｜DSML｜ invoke`.
  - A cut inside the opener itself (`\n\n<｜DSML｜ ca`) was emitted as text directly.
- **Why only `IncompleteToolCall` at `length`:**
  - `finish()` knows that a call is unfinished, not why. At `max_tokens` the buffer holds a call that was cut off, so dropping it is safe: there is no tool call, `finish_reason` stays `length`, and the client can retry with a larger `max_tokens`.
  - On any other finish reason, the buffer may hold malformed output (for example a missing `</｜DSML｜ invoke>`), and falling back keeps it visible. The same holds for other parser errors.
  - The drop is logged with `warn!` and the dropped length.
- **Scope:**
  - Only the DSML parser returns the new variant, so only DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1 change.
  - Other parsers that report `incomplete … tool call` with `ParsingFailed` keep their current behaviour. They can switch to `IncompleteToolCall` in follow-ups, for example Gemma4, GLM, Kimi or MiniMax.
  - The error message text is unchanged, so the existing V3.2 tests that check it pass unmodified.
- **Known, unchanged:** on `main`, `CombinedParser::finish` discards output produced earlier in the same `finish()` call when the tool parser fails. This PR does not change that, and it does not trigger for DeepSeek: its reasoning parser flushes only reasoning or only content at finish. The combined test above covers this path.
- **Other open PRs:** the Rust DSML PRs #56302, #56334 and #58057 keep the `finish()` error for an open block, so they do not overlap with this change. #58057 composes with it.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation above.

detail.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Drop an incomplete DeepSeek DSML tool call at max_tokens instead of leaking it into content

files.patch:
@@ -13,6 +13,12 @@ pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, ToolParserError>;
 pub enum ToolParserError {
     #[error("tool parser parsing failed: {message}")]
     ParsingFailed { message: String },
+    /// The output ended inside a tool call, so the call cannot be completed.
+    ///
+    /// Callers may treat this differently from other parse errors; see the
+    /// unified output path in the chat crate.
+    #[error("tool parser parsing failed: {message}")]
+    IncompleteToolCall { message: String },
     #[error(
         "`{name}` only provides a unified parser; the same reasoning parser and tool parser should be specified together"
     )]
